# The DPO loss and its implicit reward

## The loss (Eq. 7, page 4)

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{DPO}}(\pi_\theta;\pi_{\text{ref}}) = -\,\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[\log\sigma\!\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_w\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_w\mid x)} - \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y_l\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y_l\mid x)}\right)\right]
$$

The terms are:
- $y_w$ is the preferred completion and $y_l$ is the dispreferred one (page 3).
- $\sigma$ is the logistic function (page 3).
- $\beta$ controls how far the policy may deviate from the reference policy $\pi_{\text{ref}}$, which is normally the SFT model (page 4).

## What plays the role of the reward

The reward is the scaled log-ratio between the policy and the reference model:

$$
\hat r_\theta(x,y) = \beta\log\frac{\pi_\theta(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)}
$$

The paper calls this "the reward implicitly defined by the language model $\pi_\theta$ and reference model $\pi_{\text{ref}}$" (page 5).

**Why this works.** The paper rearranges the closed-form optimal policy of the KL-constrained objective. This expresses any reward in terms of its optimal policy (Eq. 5, page 4):

$$
r(x,y) = \beta\log\frac{\pi_r(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)} + \beta\log Z(x)
$$

The Bradley-Terry model depends only on the difference between two rewards. When this expression is substituted into it, the partition function $Z(x)$ cancels (page 4). The loss therefore has the same form as the reward-model loss in Eq. 2, where $\mathcal{L}_R = -\mathbb{E}[\log\sigma(r_\phi(x,y_w) - r_\phi(x,y_l))]$ (page 3). The only change is that $r_\phi$ is replaced by the implicit reward. The paper describes this as fitting "an implicit reward using an alternative parameterization, whose optimal policy is simply $\pi_\theta$" (page 4). This is also the meaning of the title claim that "the policy network represents both the language model and the (implicit) reward" (page 4; Section 5.1, page 5).

**No loss of generality.** Theorem 1 states that, under mild assumptions, every reward equivalence class consistent with Plackett-Luce or Bradley-Terry can be represented as $\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)}$ for some model $\pi$ (page 6). The proof is in Appendix A.6 (page 18).

**In code.** The PyTorch implementation computes this reward as `rewards = beta * (pi_logps - ref_logps).detach()`, next to `losses = -F.logsigmoid(beta * (pi_logratios - ref_logratios))` (page 20).
